data: A 10-minute walkthrough from install to your first verified report. No technical background needed.
This walkthrough takes you from zero to your first verified report. It stays practical on purpose: install, index, ask, read, repeat.

Spinosa needs the CLI and a folder of source documents.

# One command installs everything
curl -fsSL https://github.com/TommasoPrinetti/spinosa/releases/download/stable/install.sh | bash

# Create a workspace from your document folder
spinosa new

The CLI asks you to choose your document folder, name the workspace, and confirm what it found. When it finishes, it prints a startup prompt for your LLM tool.

Copy that startup prompt and run it. This is the one-time setup pass that prepares the workspace for research. What you'll notice:

  • Spinosa reads the converted files in raw/
  • It builds the dictionary and navigation maps
  • It writes a startup report so you can confirm indexing completed cleanly Typical startup time is a few minutes for small corpora and longer for large, mixed-format collections.

Once startup finishes, ask a plain-language research question in your LLM tool. Example:

What did the Normandy interviews say about coastal erosion? Spinosa then searches the corpus, assembles evidence, drafts an answer, and verifies the result against the source text before handing the report back.

Every answer comes back as a markdown report in agent_reports/. The report gives you:

  • A direct answer to the question
  • Evidence quotes with source paths
  • Analysis that separates interpretation from source text
  • Limitations so you can judge scope and confidence
  • A verification status showing whether the claims passed source checks For the full anatomy of a report, including statuses and charts, use Reports & Charts.

After the first report, the normal loop is simple:

  1. Ask a narrower follow-up or a broader comparison.
  2. Review the cited files in raw/ if you want to inspect the evidence directly.
  3. Add new documents when the corpus changes, then refresh the workspace. If you want to understand what the agents are doing behind the scenes, read Agents & Pipeline. If you want the file layout and workspace internals, read Corpus Structure.

• Agents & Pipeline for how questions are routed and verified
  • Corpus Structure for the workspace layout and index files
  • CLI Reference for commands like prepare, check, and update
  • FAQ if startup or report generation is misbehaving
